family.tagline: A first house, a family office corner, and a quiet Core.
family.story: Caleb works delivery shifts and Daniela keeps books part time. They bought their first house with Luca and Maya in tow. The Companion Core sits in the family office corner of the bedroom.

companion.name: Gil
companion.job: Turns the week's shift messages into a family plan Caleb edits.
companion.limits: Proposes a plan. Caleb confirms every shift.

companion.name: Pepper
companion.job: Opens Wallos in its own browser and lists the subscriptions that renew this week.
companion.limits: Reads the list. Daniela decides what to keep.

popup.title: A parcel for the front stoop
popup.body: A parcel waits on the front stoop. Caleb, home from an early shift, carries it through the vestibule to the family office corner in the bedroom.

popup.title: The family opens the parcel
popup.body: Luca does the unwrapping. Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. It covers about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plugged in at the corner desk
popup.body: Daniela plugs in the cable behind the desk and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Pick the home network
popup.body: Caleb joins the Core's own Wi-Fi network from his phone, then picks the home network.

popup.title: Starter agents, starter apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Daniela picks OpenClaw and Caleb picks Hermes. They add Companion Memory (beta), Wallos and Yuvomi, then walk away.

beats.capability: an agent with its own browser and coding tools, running in its own sandbox

popup.title: Pepper checks in
popup.body: Daniela sends the first message to Pepper, the agent she named. Pepper answers, and the Core is running.

say.speaker: daniela
say.text: Hi, Daniela. I am Pepper. Which list first?

beats.capability: track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Pepper reads the renewal list
popup.body: Daniela asks Pepper which subscriptions renew this week. Pepper opens Wallos in its own browser and lists them. Daniela decides what to keep.

say.speaker: daniela
say.text: Here is the list. You decide what to keep.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host. Works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Sign-ins in one vault
popup.body: Every password the family shares goes into VaultWarden, a vault hosted on the Core beside Daniela's chair. It works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: invoicing, expenses, customers and profit and loss for a small business

popup.title: A client's books, kept here
popup.body: On Tuesdays, Daniela keeps a client's books in Akaunting: invoices, expenses and customers. The records sit on the Core.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: The house papers, searchable
popup.body: Daniela scans the closing papers for the new house into Paperless-ngx. It reads every page, tags it and makes the lot searchable.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores

popup.title: Pantry first, then the shop
popup.body: Before the weekly shop, Caleb checks the pantry in Grocy. It tracks what is on the shelves and keeps the shopping list.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Gil turns shifts into a plan
popup.body: Caleb texts Gil the week's shifts. Gil drafts a family plan, and Caleb confirms every shift in Yuvomi.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: caleb
say.text: Here is the plan as a draft. Please check every shift.

beats.capability: track accounts, budgets, bills and savings goals, with rules that sort your transactions

popup.title: Month end, sorted by rules
popup.body: At the dining table, Daniela imports the month's statement as a CSV file into Firefly III. Its rules sort the transactions.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: A birthday card for abuela
popup.body: Caleb writes a birthday card for Luca's abuela in English. LibreTranslate turns it into Spanish, and Daniela checks every line.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: The same cartoon, again
popup.body: Saturday morning, Luca asks for the same cartoon again. Jellyfin plays it on the living-room TV from the family's library on the Core.

beats.capability: browse and share your photo library, with automatic tagging

popup.title: The year's photos, tagged
popup.body: On the couch after a late shift, Caleb scrolls the year's photos in PhotoPrism. It tags them as they arrive, with no upload anywhere.

beats.capability: one start page for your apps

popup.title: One start page for the family
popup.body: By the front door, Caleb sets Homarr as the family's start page. The apps on the Core sit together there, one tap from any phone.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off

popup.title: Maya's bear story, resumed
popup.body: At bedtime, Maya asks for the bear story. Audiobookshelf starts it where it stopped, from the library on the Core.

beats.capability: turn habits and chores into a game with levels and quests

popup.title: Shoes away earns a level
popup.body: Luca puts his shoes away, and Daniela taps the check in Habitica. The game gives him a level, and the list lives on the Core.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds

popup.title: The tomatoes keep a diary
popup.body: Luca waters the tomato plants. Daniela logs the date in HortusFox, so no one has to remember.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: Clips waiting after a late shift
popup.body: The family's IP camera looks at the front stoop. Frigate keeps the clips on the Core, and Caleb checks them on the home Wi-Fi after a late shift.

popup.title: One Core, one first house
popup.body: The Ramos-Whitfield household runs its renewals, shifts and photos from one Core in the family office corner.

closing.body: Your renewals, your photos and your family plan can sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: FTUE follows the owner's hotspot flow (STORY-BIBLE section 7); owner sign-off against the fact sheet is still open.
The Core stands in the family bedroom: told as the family office corner in the FTUE and the first room chapter, never as a server in a bedroom.
A budget-conscious family: no saving, payback or price claim anywhere. Wallos is a subscription list, Firefly III a bookkeeping tool fed by a CSV file.
garden-stoop assumes the family owns an IP camera (not in the Core parcel, not in the 3D scene). No claim that it prevents anything.
Mealie (a signature app) is not used: it has no QA screenshot. Invented place and street: check Pecan Weir and Poppy Seed Lane against a map.
